overview: Rowe's 1937 despatch explains Japan's postal, telegraph, telephone, and shipping-mail laws applied in Taiwan with only minor local administrative variations; State later transmitted copies to the Commerce Department and Federal Communications Commission.

subfiles.title: Despatch on communications laws applicable in Taiwan
subfiles.from: Alvin T. Rowe, Jr., American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports on whether Taiwan had special local communications laws distinct from those of Japan proper.
subfiles.summary: Rowe confirms, per Government General officials, that Imperial ordinances extended Japanese communications laws to Taiwan under local Ordinance No. 80, with only minor administrative differences, concluding separate translations of local decrees were unnecessary.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Taihoku despatch to the Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of the June 7 despatch concerning Taiwan's communications laws.
subfiles.summary: State forwards Commerce a copy of Rowe's 1937 Taihoku despatch No. 17 on Taiwan's communications laws.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Taihoku despatch to the Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: The Acting Chairman of the Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.about: Transmits the June 7 Taihoku despatch to the Law Department of the Federal Communications Commission.
subfiles.summary: State sends the FCC's Acting Chairman Rowe's despatch No. 17 on Taiwan's communications laws, for its Law Department.

interest: Shows Taiwan's incorporation into Japan's communications-law regime, circulated to Commerce and the FCC.
